grounds: The ferry was eleven hours late because of a crew strike. We paid for our first night in Bologna in advance and could not use it, and that is a direct result of the delay. I don't accept that it is a consequential loss.
reason: The prepaid night in Bologna was lost because the delay made it impossible to arrive on the day booked, and the policy does not clearly tell a customer that such a cost is left out. The insurer should pay the cost of the night and a modest sum for the inconvenience, with interest.

grounds: Our passports were lost on the drive to the port, the day before the cruise. We were on the trip to the cruise port and I think our cover started when we left home. It's unfair to refuse us over one day.
reason: The policy describes the covered trip by its dates but also as the journey you take to your departure, and a customer could reasonably read the cover as starting when they leave home. That ambiguity should be resolved in the customer's favour. The insurer should pay the replacement costs, compensation for the distress on embarkation day, and interest.

grounds: The physiotherapy was prescribed by the hospital doctor in Costa Rica after the injury. It is part of treating the injury, not something extra, and I was told by the insurer's phone line that it would be covered.
reason: The hospital's discharge note prescribed the physiotherapy as part of the treatment of the injury, and the policy does not say that care after the customer returns home is excluded. The insurer should pay the physiotherapy, with interest.

grounds: I saw my doctor about my back in April, which is before the 60 days. The dose of my tablets went up in May but I had no new symptoms and no referral. I don't think that is a pre-existing condition.
reason: The policy asks about changes in treatment in the 60 days before purchase and says so clearly. The dose of the customer's medicine was increased for continuing back pain inside that period, and the herniated disc is linked to it. The insurer applied the exclusion fairly and the complaint is not upheld.

grounds: The flights were cancelled, we could not travel and we lost the cost of the trip. We had no idea the storm would hit when we bought the policy, since the forecast was still uncertain.
reason: The storm had been named and was forecast to reach the destination the day before the policy was bought. The policy tells customers that events publicly known before purchase are not covered, and the insurer was entitled to rely on that. The complaint is not upheld.

grounds: Everything in the bag was stolen and I have the receipts. The insurer paid $1,500 of $3,176 and I think I should be paid what I lost.
reason: The policy states a maximum of $1,500 for baggage on this plan, and it was drawn to the customer's attention in the policy summary. The insurer paid the maximum, so there is nothing further to pay. The complaint is not upheld.

grounds: The insurer cut my claim for the laptop to $300 and paid only part of what I lost. The laptop cost far more than that and the limit was never explained to me when I bought the policy.
I missed the Montserrat excursion only because my passport was lost, so the cost of it follows directly from the loss. I think it should be paid with the rest.
